correctness.rationale: Gauge invariance of a positive unilateral shift reduces the numerical radius to half the top Jacobi adjacency eigenvalue. For E=2cosh κ above [-2,2], left recurrence with x_-1=0 gives sinh((j+1)κ), the right ℓ² solution is exp(-kκ), and two exceptional-edge equations yield t²-1=(exp(2κ)-1)/(1-exp(-2Lκ)). This increases strictly from 1/L, proving the exact threshold and unique positive outlier; the essential edge is not an ℓ² state. With κ=y_L/L, compact monotone-root convergence gives y_L→yβ defined by β=2y/(1-exp(-2y)); cosh expansion gives L²(ω-1)→yβ²/2. Left Riemann sums and exact right geometric norm, plus dominated exponential tails, give strong L² normalized eigenvector convergence and the stated left-mass hyperbolic ratio. Independently checked threshold and continuum scaling at several β and L; checks supplement the analytic proof.

final_claim: For a unilateral Hilbert-space weighted shift with one positive exceptional edge at depth L, a discrete band-edge outlier emerges iff t²>1+1/L. Along t²=1+β/L, β>1, the outlier has an exact inverse-square scaling limit and its L²-normalized eigenfunction converges strongly to a sinh/exponential continuum boundary layer with an exact left-mass fraction.
limitations: Single positive edge perturbation, Hilbert-space numerical radius, β>1 fixed for the normalized eigenstate; no eigenfunction at or below threshold.
Strong convergence not uniform as β↓1; diagnostic numerics alone cannot certify the infinite-dimensional claim.
